title: Anchor account technical sprint pocket deck
summary: Compact, engineer-friendly slide deck for seller + SE to run a technical sprint with an anchor account pilot. Focus: rapid validation, clear fallbacks, SLA economics, and canary rollback checklist.
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Single-sheet pocket deck for sellers and sales engineers to run a 3-session technical sprint with an anchor account (executive sponsor + platform engineer + product owner).
- Audience: AE, SE, Solutions Eng, Customer Success lead.
- Goal: convert pilot -> paid Dedicated or Private deployment within 90 days, with clear success metrics and rollback safety net.

Why a compact sprint deck?
- Anchor accounts require low friction, clear risk mitigation, and ops-safe demos that map directly to procurement/security checks.
- This deck minimizes slide noise and surfaces only what influences procurement, SRE sign-off, and early ROI metrics.

Sprint overview (3 sessions):
- Session 0 (pre-sprint): 45m discovery call (stakeholders + infra). Deliverable: runbook + security checklist.
- Session 1 (pilot scope + quick-boot): 2h hands-on with integration architect and SE — validate connectivity, token flow, and 1st API call. Deliverable: smoke test results and perf baseline.
- Session 2 (scale & SLA): 3h ops deep-dive — throughput test on representative dataset, fallback policies, and canary plan. Deliverable: SLA proposal + economics snapshot.

Priority checklist (must clear before pilot kick):
- Customer provides a network diagram + allowlist (IP ranges, egress rules).
- Model family preference and sample prompt set (5–10 canonical prompts).
- Data residency needs and any PII constraints (KMS/HSM requirements).
- Contract owner identified and procurement touchpoint scheduled.

Technical success criteria (example metrics to inscribe into pilot SOW):
- 95th percentile latency <= X ms for production prompt set (define with customer).
- Steady-state throughput of Y requests/minute with <1% error rate for 30m window.
- Cost-per-1000-tokens estimate within agreed budget envelope (baseline run + 20% buffer).
- Quality threshold: red-teamed prompt set pass-rate >= 90% (customer-defined acceptance).

Demo & integration script (SE speaker notes):
- 2-minute pitch: business outcome -> short arch -> why Redwood (predictable throughput + fallbacks).
- Live demo sequence: 1) auth flow + first token, 2) short prompt generation, 3) streaming response verified, 4) failover to lower-cost variant (show response time delta).
- Show the Console: per-route token breakdown, tracing link, and rollout toggle. Point to a single console row for the demo to keep attention.

Objection & quick rebut scripts (battlecard style):
- "We can run this ourselves cheaper." -> "Yes, you can, but ask what you’re trading off: predictable latency under burst, engineering ops cost, and safe rollbacks. We provide a runtime plus guardrails so your team ships features not infra."
- "We need on-prem only." -> "We support Private + VPC deployments; we’ll map the onboarding timeline and KMS integration steps in the SOW. For speed, recommend a hybrid pilot (VPC-hosted control plane)."
- "Latency spikes are risky for UX." -> "We offer routing policies (latency-first), prefix/KV caching for common prompts, and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants. Let’s show a canary policy now."

Canary & rollback checklist (ops-focused):
- Canary group selection: 1% traffic, single region, no sensitive data paths.
- Monitoring hooks: 99/95/50 pctl latency, error rate, quality regression alerts wired to Slack/#pilot-alerts.
- Auto-fallback policy: degrade to cached results for qualified routes or route to cheaper variant.
- Rollback steps: 1) disable canary; 2) route all traffic to fallback variant; 3) open incident runbook; 4) post-mortem owner assigned.

SLO and pricing quick-frame (for negotiation):
- Basic: best-effort with soft SLOs (useful for POC).
- Production: 99.9% availability SLA, 95th pctl latency target (customer-agreed).
- Billing constructs to propose: usage + reserved commit (3-month pilot commit recommended to secure capacity).

Risk matrix (one slide):
- Network gating -> Mitigation: pre-sprint network diagram + test VPN.
- Model quality unknowns -> Mitigation: sample-label pass + early eval harness.
- Cost overrun -> Mitigation: token budget cap + alert on burn rate.

Engineering appendix (for SEs):
- Quick commands (curl examples) — auth header, streaming response, error codes to expect.
- Prompts to test cache hit behavior (prefix-heavy, repetitive sequences).
- Suggested batch sizes and concurrency knobs for Dedicated pools.

Customer-facing pilot SOW template (short):
- Scope: endpoints, model family, token estimate, security constraints.
- Timeline: Kick -> 0–2 weeks (setup) -> 2–4 weeks (validate) -> 4–8 weeks (scale & handoff).
- Accept criteria: signed checklist from engineering + product owner.
- Exit options: extend pilot, convert to reserved capacity, or hand back with recommended infra configs.

Playbook folding for AE/SE handoff:
- Immediately after Session 1: upload network diagram + smoke report to linked Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-4201).
- After Session 2: prepare a short one-pager for procurement with the SLA and cost estimate (attach to opportunity in Salesforce).

Actionable one-liners for seller conversations:
- "We’ll run a 2-week smoke test with 0 production risk and a clear rollback—no surprise costs, just measurable SLA targets."
- "If you want complete isolation, we can show an on-prem timeline and a hybrid pilot to unblock security reviews faster."

Open questions to capture in discovery:
- Do you have a token budget cap for pilots?
- Which teams must sign security approval (names/roles)?
- Any compliance controls beyond SOC2/HIPAA?

Appendix: checklist for internal readiness before seller reaches out:
- SE sandbox environment pre-provisioned with at least one Dedicated slot.
- Playbook link and brief recorded demo (3–4 min).
- Engineering on-call for pilot week confirmed and contactable.

Notes to self (working):
- Consider adding a short 'customer elevator' card for finance stakeholders (CFO-focused cost vs. risk bullets).
- Add a pre-built evaluation harness that auto-runs customer prompts and outputs a quality vs. latency heatmap. Task: GitHub PR linking harness.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-4201 (pilot templates), JIRA-GTM-876 (anchor account play tweaks), GitHub PR: pilot-scripts/pull/34 (automation for smoke tests).

Origin: created as a compact seller/SE kit after Friday workshop with Platform Sellers and SE leads. This is intentionally lean — focus on running safe, measurable pilots with anchor customers and turning them into committed capacity deals.

(End of pocket deck)
